findings.title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a brand-new logger, discarding recorded logs
findings.body: `TestLogger.FromContext` returns `NewTestLogger()` instead of a logger that shares the receiver's `DebugLogs/InfoLogs/WarnLogs/ErrorLogs` counters. Since `LoggerMiddleware.logRequest` now emits its log line via `m.logger.FromContext(ctx).Info(...)`, any test that injects a `*TestLogger` into the middleware and then asserts on `logger.InfoLogs.Calls`/`Message`/`Ctx` will observe zero calls — the log is recorded on a throwaway instance. This silently makes log assertions for the logger middleware (and any other code that logs through `FromContext`) impossible, so regressions in the log output will go undetected. The fake should return the same instance (or one sharing the `Logs` structs).

findings.title: Logger middleware silently depends on ContextualLoggerMiddleware being installed above it
findings.body: `logRequest` no longer adds `pluginId`, `endpoint`, `uname`, `dsName`, `dsUID` or `traceID` to the log parameters; it relies entirely on `m.logger.FromContext(ctx)` picking up the attributes injected by the new `ContextualLoggerMiddleware` (and, for `traceID`, on the tracing package having registered a contextual log provider). This dependency is implicit and unchecked: if `NewLoggerMiddleware` is used without `NewContextualLoggerMiddleware`, or if the two are ordered so that the contextual middleware runs after the logger middleware, the 'Plugin Request Completed' lines degrade to just status/duration with no plugin, datasource, user or trace identification — a silent loss of operational data. Consider adding the key fields back explicitly, or documenting/enforcing the ordering requirement (and covering it with a test).

findings.title: ContextualLoggerMiddleware dereferences req without nil checks
findings.body: `QueryData`, `CallResource`, `CheckHealth` and `CollectMetrics` access `req.PluginContext` unconditionally. The sibling `LoggerMiddleware` in the same package explicitly guards `if req == nil { return m.next... }`, which indicates nil requests are considered possible in this chain; with this new middleware sitting above the logger middleware, such a request would panic here instead of being forwarded. Add the same nil guards for consistency and robustness.

findings.title: FromContext silently drops contextual attributes when the type assertion fails
findings.body: `grafanaInfraLogWrapper.FromContext` asserts the result of `d.l.FromContext(ctx)` to `*log.ConcreteLogger` and, on failure, falls back to `d.New()` — a logger with no contextual attributes at all. If `infra/log` ever returns a different `Logger` implementation, all plugin request logs would quietly lose pluginId/endpoint/traceID context with no warning. Prefer wrapping the returned `log.Logger` interface (or at least logging/annotating the fallback) rather than silently discarding the contextual logger.

findings.title: No tests for the new ContextualLoggerMiddleware
findings.body: The newly added middleware is responsible for all plugin/datasource/user attributes that now appear in the plugin request logs, but there is no test asserting that `instrumentContext` puts `endpoint`, `pluginId`, `dsName`, `dsUID` and `uname` into the context for each endpoint. Given that the logger middleware lost its explicit field list in the same PR, a regression here would silently drop these fields from logs with nothing failing in CI.

findings.title: Test name still refers to the removed InstrumentationMiddleware
findings.body: The test function is still called `TestInstrumentationMiddleware` while the middleware it exercises is now `MetricsMiddleware` (`newMetricsMiddleware`). Since the whole point of the PR is the rename, leaving the stale name makes the test hard to locate and contradicts the new naming.

findings.title: Logger name 'plugin.instrumentation' not updated after the rename
findings.body: `NewLoggerMiddleware(cfg, log.New("plugin.instrumentation"))` keeps the old 'instrumentation' naming, so emitted log lines are tagged with a logger name that no longer corresponds to any middleware in the code (instrumentation was split into metrics + contextual logger + logger middlewares). Operators grepping logs by logger name will be misled; rename it to something like 'plugin.logger' / 'plugin.request'.
